description.value: The study used fMRI to examine neural and subjective cue reactivity to tobacco versus control advertisements in smokers and never-smokers, and assessed whether nicotine-dependence severity modulated neuronal cue reactivity.

spans.text: In the present study, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to assess the neural processing of tobacco advertisements in nicotine-dependent smokers and never-smokers.

value: The analysis revealed solely negative correlations: less nicotine-dependent smokers revealed higher cue-elicited activations throughout all brain lobes. The negative correlation of cue-elicited brain activation and severity of dependence was most pronounced in limbic areas and the thalamus.

spans.text: Concerning the association between severity of nicotine dependence and neuronal cue reactivity in the group of smokers our analysis revealed solely negative correlations, i.e. less nicotine-dependent smokers revealed higher cue-elicited activations throughout all brain lobes.
